semantics.points: Fin 100 = {0, ..., 99} with addition modulo 100 (Fin.add); PC100.shift 100 = Equiv.addRight 1, i.e. x ↦ x + 1 (root shift100_apply: rfl).
semantics.design: IsDesign241 B := (∀ X ∈ B, X.card = 4) ∧ ∀ T, T.card = 2 → ∃! X, X ∈ B ∧ T ⊆ X.  B is a set of blocks (a repeated block would put its pairs in two blocks).
semantics.parallel_class: IsParallelClass B P := P ⊆ B ∧ ∀ y, ∃! X, X ∈ P ∧ y ∈ X (blocks of B partitioning the points).
semantics.resolution: IsResolution B R := (∀ P ∈ R, IsParallelClass B P) ∧ ∀ X ∈ B, ∃! P, P ∈ R ∧ X ∈ P (R partitions B into parallel classes).
semantics.automorphism: IsResolutionAutomorphism B R σ := B.image (blockImage σ) = B ∧ ∀ P ∈ R, P.image (blockImage σ) ∈ R, blockImage σ X = X.map σ.toEmbedding: σ maps the block set onto itself and every class onto a class.
semantics.cycle: IsFullCycle σ := σ.IsCycle ∧ σ.support = Finset.univ (Mathlib IsCycle and support): σ permutes all points in one cycle.  root100_cycleType: cycleType of x ↦ x + 1 on Fin 100 is {100}.
semantics.targets: Target 100 := ∃ B, IsDesign241 B ∧ ∃ R, IsResolution B R ∧ ∃ σ, IsFullCycle σ ∧ IsResolutionAutomorphism B R σ (TZ 2026 Def. 5).  TargetShift 100 := IsFullCycle (shift 100) ∧ ∃ B R, IsDesign241 B ∧ IsResolution B R ∧ IsResolutionAutomorphism B R (shift 100).  TargetCounts 100 adds B.card = 825, R.card = 33, P.card = 25 (as v(v-1)/12, (v-1)/3, v/4).
semantics.witness: pc100Blocks = blocks 100 cert100 = {blk 100 e : e listed}, pc100Classes = classes 100 cert100 = {classOf 100 c : c a raw class}, blk e = {e.1, e.2.1, e.2.2.1, e.2.2.2} mod 100 (pc100Blocks_spec, pc100Classes_spec).  witness100 proves IsDesign241, IsResolution, IsResolutionAutomorphism (shift 100), IsFullCycle (shift 100) and the counts 825 / 33 / 25 for these explicit objects.
semantics.binding: cert100 is the raw certificate (SHA-256 971f…4f7c1) copied verbatim in raw order by gen_lean.py (replay step 2 regenerates it byte-identically); cert100_range (kernel) shows every number is below 100, so no reduction modulo 100 occurs.  audit_binding.py (replay step 3) checks literal = certificate, that the Theorem C expansion of the compact seed (SHA-256 ac72…6245) is byte-identical to the certificate, and that the Lean objects recomputed from the literal are the certificate blocks and classes.  The Lean theorems do not mention the raw files; the raw-to-object equality is this external stdlib audit.
semantics.not_hypotheses: The pair coverage, the class partitions, the shift invariance and the counts are not hypotheses of any root: they are kernel evaluations (cert100_check, cert100_shape, cert100_range by decide +kernel) fed to the data-independent soundness theorem sound_of_check; the cycle facts come from Mathlib (isCycle_finRotate, support_finRotate, cycleType_finRotate).
